repeats.why: Three cards in one chapter are the same question: a friend shows you something that isn't good (the song, the haircut, the crush with a red flag). The answer sets are the same four moves each time: say it now, hype it, praise something else, bring it up later in private. C2-8 'DMs later' and C2-10 'bring up the flag later, just the two of you' are one answer. A player feels this by the second one.
repeats.fix: Keep C2-1 (golden) as the chapter opener. Move C2-10 to the finale so it sits 50 cards away. Rewrite C2-8's options as true group roles with no 'later, in private' and no 'compliment something else' move (C2-1 already owns the side-step), e.g. the one who starts the group hype, the one who asks 'was this on purpose?' out loud, the one who books them a fix-it appointment.

repeats.why: Both are 'split the cost when one side has less money', and they share the literal answer 'Fair is fair' plus 'split by what each has' = 'the ones with more cover more'. This is the exact equal-vs-proportional repeat Jerry called out in test 1.
repeats.fix: Cut C4-11. Reword C3-3 option 1 so 'Fair is fair' appears nowhere.

fatigue: Run length: 76 cards (73 for teens) against the brief's 7 to 9 per chapter and 56 to 64 total. Around card 55 (chapter 6) a player is 11 minutes in with 20 to go; test 1 showed that is where tapping without reading starts. The proposed order is 59 chapter cards plus the 8-card finale (56 plus 8 for teens).

Every chapter ends with two sealed cards back to back (C1-9/10, C2-10/11, C3-10/11, C4-10/11, C5-S1/S2, C6-S1/S2, C7-S1/S2): 7 type-rotation breaks and a rhythm the player learns by chapter 2. The brief puts sealed checks in one finale of 8.

The feeling card uses the same stem ('What showed up first?') and near-identical five emotion words 7 times. By the fourth it is a reflex tap. Keep 5 (C1-3, C2-6, C3-6, C5-8, C6-5), cut C4-6 and C7-8, and vary the stems ('Your gut, in one word?', 'First thing in your chest?').
All 11 real cards open with 'Think of the last time...'. Vary the opener ('When did you last...', 'Your most recent...', 'Remember the last...').

Chapter 4 opens with four buy-or-don't cards (jacket, sneakers, plant, the thing you already have plenty of) and closes with three split-the-money cards (C4-7, C4-9, C4-11). Money was the area where Jerry felt 'multiple of the same answer' in test 1.

Chapter 2 is 11 cards of 'a friend needs something from you': three are the same feedback question (song, haircut, red flag), three are the same rest-versus-show-up question (11:48pm, loan, couch). Samey even though every card is well written.
Chapter 5 has four L2 cards and three job-offer setups (C5-2, C5-4, C5-6); the second half reads as one long careers card.
Chapter 6 puts R3 on 6 of 11 cards and currently ends R3, R3, R3 (C6-9, C6-S1, C6-S2).

L3's three Sally scoring cards (C7-1 Q02, C7-4 Q38, C7-7 Q40) all sit in chapter 7 at minutes 10 to 12, where rushed taps count at 0.3. L3 is the axis most likely to come out 'unfinished'. Fix: the new L3 this-or-that in chapter 5 (C5-NEW-L3), plus both chapter 7 real cards moved to slots 2 and 4.

Motif and phrase repeats a player will notice: 'group chat' on about 10 cards, 'screenshot' on 5 (C1-1, C1-10, C2-3, C2-5, C5-7), 'Future me says thanks' (C4-1, C5-S1), 'Fair is fair' (C3-3, C4-11), 'already has a job / plans' (C2-9, C4-3, C4-10), 'zero guilt' (C5-S1, C7-6), 'instant noodles' (C2-2, C5-2), 'color-coded' (C1-9, C7-5). Each should appear once in the whole run.

Rule breaks in the current order: same axis or tag pair next to each other at C1-9/C1-10 (T02), C3-8/C3-9 (T11), C5-9/C5-S1 (L2, T16), C5-S1/C5-S2 (L1), C6-9/C6-S1 (R3), C6-S1/C6-S2 (R3). Chapter 6's two this-or-that cards are singles, not a round of 3. The proposed order fixes all of these except the chapter 6 singles (only 2 this-or-that cards there; C6-9 is 18+).

overall: The cards are much better than kit v1: real situations, no ladder answers, and every Sally question has a home. The run as ordered would still get Jerry's test 1 complaint, for three reasons. First, the same question comes back in new clothes: feedback to a friend three times in chapter 2; splitting money four times across chapters 3 and 4, with the literal answer 'Fair is fair' twice; privilege twice; the free afternoon twice; the holiday twice; parents want you close twice; share access with your person twice. Second, the structure is one repeating template: every chapter closes with two sealed cards, every feeling card uses the same stem, and every real card starts 'Think of the last time'. Third, it is too long (76 cards against 56 to 64) and it loads L3, the axis that needs the most care, into the last three minutes. Fix: cut 10 cards (6 sealed repeats, 2 split or privilege repeats, 2 feeling cards), move the 8 remaining sealed checks into one finale, add one early L3 this-or-that, and use the order above. Six text fixes are also needed so answers stop echoing each other: C2-8 options, C3-3 'Fair is fair', C4-3 and C2-9 'already has a job', C5-5 'tomorrow', C7-6 back to Sally Q47, C7-S1 option 3. With those done, the only same-type pair a player might notice is C4-3/C4-5 (both Sally-mandated), and they now sit 3 cards apart.
